text: The cause is confirmed: a duplicate Task, consuming the same Stream as the original. This lesson removes it correctly, cleans up what it already wrote, and proves the fix actually held.

Suspend first, not drop directly — that stops any further duplicate writes immediately, while leaving the object available a moment longer in case anything needs double-checking. SHOW TASKS confirms only the original now shows started. Only then does DROP TASK remove the duplicate for good.

The duplicate rows already written still need cleaning up. ROW_NUMBER, partitioned by ticket ID and updated_at, ordered by load time, numbers each duplicate group's rows — keeping only the first and deleting the rest leaves exactly one row per genuine refund event.

After refreshing Power BI, re-run the exact comparison from Lesson 13: refund_event_count against the distinct refunded ticket count, for every week, not just the one that was reported. They now match exactly.

Cleaning up this one incident doesn't prevent the same mistake happening again next time someone touches the pipeline. A standing duplicate-check view, expected to always return zero rows, turns a slow surprise weeks later into something a short SQL check catches immediately. Next lesson wraps up what this whole chapter built.
